$comment: Loomfall death messages. Every string is a third-person broadcast containing {player}. Kills are spoken gently — unpicked, unmade, unwound, laid straight — never gore; pity over hate. Cause ids: mob:* ids match bestiary.json entity ids exactly. 'lava' and 'explosion' are engine-facing fallback ids kept for systems compatibility — in fiction the liquid is always the molten skein (see naming.json/tips.json) and the only canon blast source is the waxling burst; builders should not invent new blast sources, and no in-game string may say 'lava'.

messages: {player} was dropped, like a stitch.
{player} came down faster than the pattern could think to catch.
{player} mistook a long way down for a short one. The ground kept every knot to itself.

deathMessages.note: Engine fallback id retained for systems compatibility; the fiction calls it the molten skein, never lava.
messages: {player} went into the molten skein and came out as someone else's color.
{player} stepped into a river of thread still deciding what to be. It decided without them.
{player} was rendered back to raw thread in the making-fire. The Cinderloom did not notice the donation.
{player} forgot that a Mender is mostly wool, and wool takes on water.
{player} went under the weave of the water and never found the surface stitch.

deathMessages.note: Engine fallback id. The only canon blast source is the waxling burst (covered under mob:waxling); this cause exists for systems compatibility, and builders should not invent new blast sources to feed it.
messages: {player} came apart all at once, which is at least tidier than slowly.
{player} was scattered past mending. The pieces remain fond of one another.
{player} ran out of thread halfway through the pattern.
{player} wound down to the bare spool. Even a Waking Thread must be fed back into itself.
{player} caught, and burned, and the smoke rose toward a Weaver who was not watching.
{player} learned that thread and fire were never meant to keep long company.
{player} stood still in the Emberwarp, which down there counts as volunteering.
{player} carried Warpwold's chill too deep, and the heat of first-making warmed them past holding.
{player} drifted past the last selvage, and the dark picked them apart with great patience.
{player} fell where a dropped thread falls forever. In a loose sort of way, they are falling still.
{player} came undone in Nevermend. The Ravelling was not unkind about it; it is only the weather there.
{player} was stitched into a needlejack's count. It stands a little taller now, and is no less wrong.
{player} stayed out past the unbending hour.
{player} was unpicked by something that is not cruel, only wrong-woven, and was never allowed to be anything else.
{player}'s thread was drawn out, slowly and sorrowfully, by hands no one ever tidied away. Do not mistake it for a victory; it is still not whole.
{player} held still one moment past the mercy of the Understruck.
{player} was worried loose at the hems. The pack politely waited until two of them could see.
{player} stopped to mend the fraying, and the second hound was already behind them.
{player} stood still while the Silence-Moths took the armor stitch by stitch, and then took the rest. None of it made a sound.
{player} was nibbled down to bare warp by things too gentle to mean it.
{player} was snared in burning silk and kept, briefly, like something precious.
{player} slowed by half, and half again, and the emberspinner came along its own line to collect.
{player} was sealed in hot tallow, like a letter no one will send.
{player} let the soft slumping thing come close enough to give everything it had.
{player} took from the forges, and an order no one ever cancelled was carried out to the letter.
{player}'s warmth was drawn out through a spindle-stave by a keeper that has already resumed its rounds, murmuring the report to an empty niche.
{player} carried the cold of home into the Wastes, and the slagmoths came to fix it.
{player} was warmed all the way through, inside their own armor, by things that only wanted the chill gone.
{player} was wound onto the First Bobbin and fed to a fire that still believes the Weaver is coming back.
{player} became new thread for a work that cannot finish. The First Bobbin did not stop turning.
{player} was taken apart, thread by borrowed thread, by something trying to be whole again. It is still not. Nothing marks the spot.
{player} was gathered in by The Unpicked, and the pattern has already forgotten what they carried.
{player} dangled, for one moment, like untidiness. A raveler came and tidied.
{player} was undone mid-grip by something that never hated what they built.
{player} raised a point against the finished edge. The hem had heard it before, and kept its answer wound and waiting.
{player} was laid straight along the hem, in the neat, unhurried way of a thing that has only ever had one duty and no doubt.
{player} stood on the line the Last Needle meant to unpick, and went with it. The Needle did not notice the difference.
{player} met the point of the horizon. It is not done. Neither, quite, was {player}; the anchor held.
